rmt-2004-adv-01.title: Add the corner entries
rmt-2004-adv-01.body:
$\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}1&b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&a+b\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, so the product is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1+3+5+\cdots+99\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$. The sum of the first 50 odd numbers is $50^2=2500$.

**Answer: $\begin{pmatrix}1&2500\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$**

rmt-2004-adv-02.title: Convert and expand
rmt-2004-adv-02.body:
$-\frac1{10}+\frac19-\frac18+\frac17=\frac{73}{2520}$. To get base-6 digits, repeatedly multiply the fractional part by 6 and take the integer part: $\frac{73}{2520}\to0$ (remainder $\frac{73}{420}$), $\to1$ (remainder $\frac3{70}$), $\to0$ (remainder $\frac9{35}$), $\to1$ (remainder $\frac{19}{35}$), $\to3$ (remainder $\frac9{35}$ again). The remainder $\frac9{35}$ repeats, so the digits 13 repeat forever.

**Answer: $.010\overline{13}_6$**

rmt-2004-adv-03.title: Reduce the angles
rmt-2004-adv-03.body:
$\sin100^\circ=\cos10^\circ$. $1000^\circ=280^\circ+2\cdot360^\circ$ and $10000^\circ=280^\circ+27\cdot360^\circ$, so both sines equal $\sin280^\circ=-\cos10^\circ$. The sum is $2\cos10^\circ+\cos10^\circ-\cos10^\circ-\cos10^\circ=\cos10^\circ=\sin80^\circ$.

**Answer: $x=80$**

rmt-2004-adv-05.title: Symmetry
rmt-2004-adv-05.body:
There are $8!$ arrangements and the four letters W, I, S, E appear in each of their $4!$ relative orders equally often, so $\frac{8!}{4!}=8\cdot7\cdot6\cdot5=1680$.

**Answer: 1680**

rmt-2004-adv-05.title: Choose positions
rmt-2004-adv-05.body:
Choose the 4 positions for W, I, S, E: $\binom84=70$, which fixes their order; arrange the other 4 letters in $4!=24$ ways: $70\cdot24=1680$.

**Answer: 1680**

rmt-2004-adv-07.title: Expected waiting time
rmt-2004-adv-07.body:
Let $X$ ($Y$) be the expected number of further days until Chris is king when Adam (Bill) is king. Then $X=1+\frac X3+\frac Y3$ and $Y=1+\frac X2+\frac Y4$. From the second, $Y=\frac43+\frac{2X}3$; substituting, $\frac49X=\frac{13}9$, so $X=\frac{13}4$. Adam is king on day 1, so Chris first becomes king on day $1+\frac{13}4=\frac{17}4$ in expectation.

**Answer: $\frac{17}4$**

rmt-2004-adv-09.title: Count intersections
rmt-2004-adv-09.body:
Both sides are even, so count $x>0$ and double ($x=0$ is not a solution). Write $\cos x=\frac{x^2}{2004}$; we need $x<\sqrt{2004}\approx44.8$. Each full period $[2\pi(n-1),2\pi n]$ on which $\frac{x^2}{2004}<1$ throughout gives 2 crossings; this holds for $n=1,\ldots,7$ since $\frac{(14\pi)^2}{2004}\approx0.97<1$. That gives $14$ solutions, plus exactly one more in $[14\pi,15\pi]$ (cosine decreases from 1 to $-1$ while $\frac{x^2}{2004}$ increases from below 1). Beyond $15\pi$, $\frac{x^2}{2004}>1$. So 15 positive solutions and $30$ in total. A numerical scan confirms 30.

**Answer: 30**

rmt-2004-adv-10.title: Position of the first ace
rmt-2004-adv-10.body:
Cards are drawn without replacement from a standard 52-card deck, and Allen wins when the first ace is in an odd position. Count placements of the four aces: if the first ace is in position $k$, the other three are among the later $52-k$ positions, giving $\binom{52-k}3$ ways. Summing over odd $k$: $\sum_{k\text{ odd}}\binom{52-k}3=\binom{51}3+\binom{49}3+\cdots+\binom33=140725$. Divide by $\binom{52}4=270725$: $\frac{140725}{270725}=\frac{433}{833}$.

**Answer: $\frac{433}{833}$**
